column1: Pulse the flour and 1 tsp salt in a food processor. Whisk 4 eggs with 3 tbsp water, then drizzle in with the processor running until a ball forms. Let it run 1–2 minutes more.
Knead the dough 4–5 minutes, wrap in plastic, and rest 1 hour.
Meanwhile, mix the ricotta, 1 egg, pecorino, parmesan, salt and pepper for the filling.

Cut the dough into 8 pieces, keeping the rest wrapped. Roll one into a rectangle, pass it through a pasta machine on the widest setting, fold in thirds and repeat, then pass through each setting down to the thinnest.
Whisk the remaining egg with 1 tbsp water for the egg wash.

Lightly mark 2-inch rounds on half the sheet, spoon a heaping tablespoon of filling onto each, brush around the filling with egg wash, fold the dough over, press out any air and seal. Cut out the ravioli and repeat with the remaining dough.
Boil the ravioli in well-salted water until they float and are cooked through, 3–4 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat, add the pepper and 1/4 cup pasta water, and simmer 1 minute.
Transfer the ravioli to the skillet with a slotted spoon, add the pecorino and toss, adding more pasta water if needed. Season with salt and pepper.
